facts.statement: The type species Heightingtonaspis anglica was originally named Phlyctaenius anglicus by Ramsay Traquair in 1890.
facts.quote: The type species Heightingtonaspis anglica was described by Ramsay Traquair in 1890, and was initially named Phlyctaenius anglicus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Heightingtonaspis anglica was discovered on the surface in Shropshire, England, and dated to 416 million years old.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen NHMUK PAL PV P 29417 was first discovered on the surface at the Old Red Sandstone supergroup, Shropshire, England and the fossils were radiocarbon dated in situ to 416 million years old.

facts.statement: Fossils of Heightingtonaspis have also been found in the Senni Beds of Wales.
facts.quote: it has also been found in the Senni Beds of Wales.

facts.statement: Heightingtonaspis clarkei was originally named Kujdanowiaspis clarkei by Charles R. Eastman in 1907.
facts.quote: Heightingtonaspis clarkei was described by Charles R. Eastman in 1907, and was originally named Kujdanowiaspis clarkei.

facts.statement: Heightingtonaspis clarkei was reassigned to the genus Heightingtonaspis by Denison in 1978.
facts.quote: It was later revised and reassigned to the genus Heightingtonaspis by Denison in 1978.

facts.statement: Heightingtonaspis willsi was originally named Kujdanowiaspis willsi by White in 1961 and later reassigned to the genus Heightingtonaspis, which was created by White in 1969.
facts.quote: Heightingtonaspis willsi was described by White in 1961, and was originally named Kujdanowiaspis willsi, but was later reassigned to the genus Heightingtonaspis, which was created in 1969 by White.

facts.statement: Heightingtonaspis willsi was discovered in Shropshire, England, the same location as Heightingtonaspis anglica.
facts.quote: H. willsi was discovered in the same location as H. anglica, in Shropshire, England.

facts.statement: Heightingtonaspis belongs to the parent group Actinolepididae.
Heightingtonaspis is classified in the family Actinolepididae.
Heightingtonaspis is classified in the class Placodermi.
Heightingtonaspis lived during the Lochkovian stage, between 419.62 and 413.02 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lochkovian to Lochkovian (419.62 to 413.02 million years ago)
